question: In which year did the Films Division of the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting organise the first part of ‘Nrityanjali’, an online film festival on Indian Classical Dance and Maestros?
solution:
The correct answer is __**2020**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Films Division of the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting** organized the first part of the **'Nrityanjali'**, an online film festival dedicated to **Indian Classical Dance and Maestros**, in the year **2020**.
 
• The initiative was introduced during the **COVID-19 pandemic** when cultural activities were promoted through virtual platforms.
 
• 'Nrityanjali' showcased documentaries and films featuring the rich heritage of **Indian classical dance** forms such as Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Odissi, and others, along with highlighting the works of eminent maestros.
 
• This festival aimed to promote and preserve India's traditional art forms while making them accessible to a wider audience through digital mediums.
 
• The online festival was part of the broader attempt to engage audiences virtually and continue the dissemination of India's cultural richness despite the restrictions imposed by the pandemic.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Films Division of India:**

 
 
• The **Films Division** was established in **1948** by the Government of India under the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting.
 
• It is responsible for the production and distribution of documentaries, short films, and newsreels that focus on **India's culture, heritage, and social issues**.
 
• The division has played a crucial role in archiving significant events and cultural milestones in India's history.
 
 
 
• **Indian Classical Dance Forms:**
 
 
• India is home to **eight recognized classical dance forms**, including Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Manipuri, Kuchipudi, Odissi, Sattriya, and Mohiniyattam.
 
• Each dance form is deeply rooted in **spiritual and cultural traditions** and is often associated with ancient scriptures and temples.
 
• These dances are known for their intricate movements, storytelling through **expressions (abhinaya)**, and music.
 
 
 
• **Impact of COVID-19 on Cultural Activities:**
 
 
• The COVID-19 pandemic necessitated a shift to **virtual platforms** for continuing cultural events and activities.
 
• Several organizations, including the Films Division, started hosting **online festivals and webinars** to keep art and culture alive during lockdowns.
 
• Virtual events made cultural content accessible to a **global audience**, enhancing cultural exchange and appreciation.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Documenting Indian Art Forms:**
 
 
• Documentaries and films on Indian art forms play a critical role in **preserving heritage** and educating future generations.
 
• They serve as archives of knowledge, techniques, and the legacy of **renowned artists**.
 
• Such initiatives also help in promoting tourism and global recognition of India's cultural diversity.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **'Nrityanjali'** online festival is part of the Films Division's efforts to use technology for cultural engagement and education.
 
• By organizing such events, the division aims to highlight the contributions of **legendary dancers and choreographers** who have shaped India's classical dance traditions.
 
• The initiative also underscores the importance of adapting cultural practices to **modern digital platforms** to ensure their continuity and relevance.
